title: The AI Layoff Trap
abstract: arXiv:2603.20617v4 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: If AI displaces workers faster than the economy can reabsorb them, it risks eroding the consumer demand firms depend on. We show that knowing this is not enough for firms to stop it. In a competitive task-based economy, each firm captures the full cost saving from automation but bears only a fraction of the demand loss it creates in the product market; the rest falls on rivals. This demand externality traps rational firms in an automation arms race, displacing workers beyond what is collectively optimal. The mechanism harms both workers and firm owners and can survive in general equilibrium. More competition and higher AI productivity can amplify the excess. Wage adjustment, free entry, transfers, worker equity, and Coasean bargaining need not eliminate it. A Pigouvian automation tax implements the cooperative optimum. Policy should address not only the aftermath of automation but also the competitive incentives driving it.

translated_abstract: 如果AI取代工人的速度快于经济重新吸纳他们的速度，就可能侵蚀企业赖以生存的消费者需求。我们的研究表明，仅仅认识到这一点并不足以让企业停止这一进程。在一个竞争性的任务型经济中，每家企业都能独占自动化带来的全部成本节约，却只承担其在产品市场造成的需求损失中的一小部分，其余损失由竞争对手承担。这种需求外部性使理性的企业陷入自动化军备竞赛，导致工人被取代的程度超过集体最优水平。该机制同时损害工人和企业所有者的利益，并能在一般均衡中持续存在。更激烈的竞争和更高的AI生产率会放大这种过度自动化，而工资调整、自由进入、转移支付、员工持股以及科斯式讨价还价都不一定能消除这一问题。庇古式自动化税可以实现合作最优。政策不仅应关注自动化的后果，还应关注驱动自动化的竞争激励。
tldr: 该论文提出“AI裁员陷阱”理论：由于企业独占自动化的成本节约而需求损失外溢给竞争对手，竞争市场中理性企业会陷入自动化军备竞赛，过度取代工人并损害劳资双方利益，唯有庇古式自动化税才能实现社会最优。
en_tdlr: This paper identifies the "AI Layoff Trap": since firms capture full automation cost savings while demand losses fall on rivals, a demand externality drives rational firms into an automation arms race that excessively displaces workers and harms both labor and capital, with only a Pigouvian automation tax achieving the cooperative optimum.
